findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt and returns data for stale cache
findings.body: The query groups by credentialId and takes the max updatedAt, but never filters by `expiresAt`. A `CalendarCache` row whose `expiresAt` is in the past will not be served by `getCachedAvailability` (which uses `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }`), yet the new UI in `CredentialActionsDropdown` will still display "Cache Status: Last updated …" for that credential. Users will see a cache status indicator for cache that is effectively dead. Either add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` to the `where` clause, or surface the cache only when not expired.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data, likely throws PrismaClientValidationError
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` ends with `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` and the comment says it is meant to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The Prisma client rejects empty `data` objects for updateMany ("data must have at least one non-relation field"), so this call will throw at runtime. Because this method runs inside the `unwatchCalendar` flow (only when there are remaining calendars), the throw will leave the unwatch in a half-completed state and the `remainingCalendars` cache will be re-fetched before updatedAt is updated — or, more likely, the user receives a confusing error from the webhook flow. Either pass a real column (e.g. `data: { updatedAt: new Date() }`) or stop calling this and rely on the existing cache-write side effects.

findings.title: No tests cover deleteCache tRPC mutation, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or the new component
findings.body: The new `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` tRPC mutation, the new `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method (including its mock), and the entire `CredentialActionsDropdown` component (including the access-control conditional rendering for delegation credentials and disabled connections) have no unit or integration tests. This PR also adds a security-relevant authorization check (`userId: user.id` in `deleteCache.handler.ts`); a regression that drops that check would be silent without a test. Add at minimum: a test that `deleteCacheHandler` rejects a credential belonging to another user, a test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` filters/doesn't filter expiresAt as intended, and a render test for the component's conditional dropdown rendering.

findings.title: Removes type-check on findMany args and over-widens updateManyByCredentialId
findings.body: Two changes to this file: (1) the change at line ~260 removes the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` so callers can now pass an object that is structurally invalid for Prisma (e.g. misspelled keys) and the compiler will no longer flag it. That weakens a type-safety net that was deliberately added with `satisfies`. (2) `updateManyByCredentialId` accepts `data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` with no constraint enforcing non-empty `data`, which is exactly how the empty-`{}` bug at `CalendarService.ts:1024` slipped in. Tighten the parameter type to a non-empty variant (e.g. a branded `AtLeastOne<Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput>`) and consider restoring the `satisfies`.
